nodeEvidence.what: `prosecutionCase.prosecutionCaseIdentifier.caseURN ? ...caseURN : ...prosecutionAuthorityReference` — a TRUTHY test, so an empty-string caseURN falls back too.
deriveCaseUrn applies the identical rule for the offence's originatingCaseUrn.

assertion: The hearing gives TFL a caseURN "TFL-URN-WINS" (the fixture has none) and leaves TVL with only its prosecutionAuthorityReference. Assert EXACTLY: (1) in the TFL document, both defendants' prosecutionCasesOrApplications[0].caseOrApplicationReference equal "TFL-URN-WINS", AND the nested offences[0].originatingCaseUrn also equals "TFL-URN-WINS" — the same rule is applied twice, in two different mappers, and both must be pinned; (2) in the TVL document, caseOrApplicationReference and originatingCaseUrn both equal "TVL298320922", the prosecutionAuthorityReference, because that case has no caseURN. The recorded control for the fallback half is recorded/base__prosecution-case, where neither case has a caseURN. Note the rule is `truthy`, not `!= null`: an empty-string caseURN falls back to the authority reference. Do NOT write the Java as Objects.requireNonNullElse(caseUrn, authorityReference) — that returns "" for an empty URN and diverges on a case this corpus does not contain. Prefer StringUtils.isNotEmpty or an explicit blank check, and say why in a comment pointing at this entry.
